design.function: acc(FP32) <= clear ? +0 : valid ? fp32_add(acc, bf16_mul(a, b)) : acc
design.rounding: round-to-nearest-even (the bf16 x bf16 product is exact in FP32; only the addition rounds)
design.subnormals: flush to zero: a subnormal bf16 input is read as zero of the same sign; a product or sum whose exact magnitude is below 2^-126 becomes zero with the sign of the exact result
design.nan: any NaN operand, inf x 0 and inf - inf give the canonical quiet NaN 0x7FC00000 (payloads and NaN signs are not propagated)
design.overflow: a product or rounded sum of magnitude >= 2^128 becomes infinity of the same sign

oracle: tb/bf16_golden.py: bf16 bit patterns decoded with ml_dtypes.bfloat16, product formed exactly in float64, FP32 addition by NumPy float32 (IEEE round-to-nearest-even), then the same flush / NaN / overflow rules as the RTL; compared as uint32 bit patterns after every MAC step

pass_criteria.bit_exact_verilator: 0 mismatching accumulator values over 10,000 random cases (seed 1234, case i = default_rng([1234, i]), each case = clear followed by 1..16 MAC steps, every step compared) plus all directed cases
pass_criteria.csv_sha256_identical: results CSV of the two simulators byte-identical
pass_criteria.random_case_count: exactly 10,000 random cases on each simulator
pass_criteria.directed_cases_present: all of: +0/-0 operands and results, +inf/-inf, NaN operand propagation, inf x 0 = NaN, inf - inf = NaN, max normal, min normal, overflow to infinity (product and sum), rounding ties to even (round-up and round-down direction), subnormal bf16 inputs, product flushed to zero, sum flushed to zero, exact cancellation to +0
pass_criteria.functional_coverage: 100 % of the bins defined in tb/test_mac_bf16.py before the run (operand classes x result classes, rounding decision incl. both tie directions, effective add / subtract, alignment-shift and normalisation-shift ranges)
pass_criteria.oracle_cross_check: the golden model agrees bit-for-bit with an independent exact-rational (fractions.Fraction) reference on >= 20,000 randomly generated MAC steps (seed 1234)
pass_criteria.negative_control: an RTL copy with the tie rule changed (round half up instead of half to even) must be reported as mismatching by the same test
pass_criteria.orfs_flow_completes: nangate45 ORFS flow (synthesis to final) finishes for mac_bf16 and for mac_int8 at the same clock = the INT8 MAC's closure clock, metrics extracted for both

reported_not_gating.timing_at_int8_clock: WNS of mac_bf16 at the INT8 MAC's closure clock (met or violated is a result, not a criterion)
reported_not_gating.ppa_table: area, power, max clock of INT8 MAC vs bf16 MAC

coverage_bins_amended.when: after the first native 300-case development run (Icarus), before any official run
coverage_bins_amended.what: 5 bins of the cross alignment-shift x normalisation-shift were removed from the bin set because they are mathematically unreachable; the criterion stays '100 % of the bins'

removed_bins.('0','none'): equal exponents: an addition always carries out, a subtraction always loses at least one leading bit
removed_bins.('0','left>=24'): two 24-bit significands with equal exponents differ by at least one ulp, so at most 23 leading bits cancel
removed_bins.('1','cancel_to_zero'): operands with different exponents cannot cancel exactly
removed_bins.('24..26','carry_out'): larger operand <= (2 - 2^-23) * 2^e, smaller < 2^(e-23): the exact sum stays below 2^(e+1)

superseded.result: 99/106 hit in the first native 300-case run (the 5 unreachable bins plus 2 reachable ones that got directed cases: cancel_left_16_exponents_differ, carry_out_far_aligned)

negative_control.bug: round half up instead of round half to even (RTL copy)

mac_int8.lock_holds: one hold for the whole flow

ppa_clock.why: closure clock of the INT8 MAC array: sweep B frontier of systolic_os on nangate45 (results/sweeps/phys.jsonl: 1.25 ns closes at 30/40/50 % utilization, 1.20 ns does not)

values.ppa_max_clock_note: max clock: fmax_reported_by_flow_mhz is OpenROAD's finish-stage fmax for core_clock in the single run at 1.25 ns (metadata finish__timing__fmax__clock__core_clock); max_clock_estimate_mhz = 1 / (period - setup WNS) of the same run. Both come from one run per design, not from a searched timing-closure frontier. wns_setup covers every constrained path including the input-to-register paths (inputs arrive 20 % into the cycle), which is why the WNS-based estimate is lower than the flow's fmax. Power is the flow's default vectorless estimate at 1.25 ns, where the bf16 MAC does not meet timing
